subject.name: Robot Money Treasury
subject.thesis_blurb: Robot Money's protocol-owned capital. Three wallets: the Primary (holds the ROBOTMONEY token, ETH, USDC, and runs the prop wallet buyback flywheel) plus two Stablecoin Strategy wallets delegated to external yield engines (Zyfai SS1, Giza SS2). Distinct from the vault contract, which holds depositor capital and is tracked as a separate subject.
structural_notes: concentrated in ROBOTMONEY token by design — the prop wallet flywheel requires protocol-owned reserves to be deployable
the LP-locked-until-2100 commitment makes protocol-owned liquidity the load-bearing piece of the buyback mechanism
Stablecoin Strategy 1 and 2 are delegated yield positions (Zyfai, Giza) — value comes from delegated-position price feeds, not ERC20 balanceOf on the wallet itself

research._comment: Curated summaries of Robot Money published research. The brief generator injects this into Athena's prompt only — research is Athena's context. Each article carries a `core` flag: core articles (methodology, frameworks, risk taxonomies, definitions) stay in Athena's context permanently. Non-core articles (quarterly reads, post-mortems on specific events) slide on a most-recent-N window. Athena's context = all core + most-recent non-core, capped at 15 total. Add `core: true` for foundational pieces; omit for time-bound ones.

articles.title: Treasury Allocation for On-Chain Businesses
articles.summary: 8-year backtest comparing regime-based 3-state allocation against HODL strategies (ETH, SP500) and stable yield, across a full market cycle.
key_findings: Regime-based allocation outperformed straight HODL on a risk-adjusted basis (higher Sharpe, lower max drawdown) across the 2018-2026 window.
Most of the alpha came from being de-risked in the 2022 drawdown phase, not from being aggressively risk-on in mania phases.
The 3-state model (risk-off / neutral / risk-on) captured most of the cycle alpha; finer-grained regimes added complexity without proportional improvement.

articles.title: Backtesting honestly: what survives when you remove hindsight
articles.summary: Discovered the regime model's inverse-correlation weighting was computed with full-history hindsight. Rebuilt it point-in-time and re-ran every comparison.
key_findings: Hindsight-weighted backtests overstated alpha by a material margin; the honest version is what the live model now uses.
The macro panel correlation signal held up under point-in-time weights; the on-chain panel signal was weaker but still directional.
Honest 8-year CAGR of the regime-based allocation is meaningfully positive but not the eye-popping figure the hindsight version produced.

articles.title: Conservative vs aggressive: combining macro and on-chain regime signals
articles.summary: Backtested two ways to combine macro + on-chain panels into a single composite — conservative (any panel off → off) vs aggressive (any panel on → on, unless contradicted).
key_findings: Conservative composite captures most of the drawdown protection with lower turnover.
Aggressive composite captures more upside in 2021-style melt-ups but produces more whipsaw losses in choppy regimes.
The current live model uses the conservative composite — costs some upside but keeps drawdowns shallower.

articles.title: Regime Detection
articles.summary: Prior art, methods, and data sources for risk-on / risk-off regime classification used by the Robot Money regime model.
key_findings: Composite is built from 18 indicators across macro (10) and on-chain (8) panels.
Each indicator is percentile-ranked over a rolling 3-year window, sign-aligned so high = risk-on, weighted by inverse correlation within panel.
Bucket thresholds: composite percentile <0.33 = risk-off, 0.33-0.67 = neutral, >0.67 = risk-on.

articles.title: Smart Contract Risks
articles.summary: Field guide to how DeFi vaults get exploited. Chronological case studies relevant to the Conservative DeFi Yield bucket's protocol selection.
key_findings: Vault exploits cluster around three patterns: oracle manipulation, reentrancy via callback hooks, and admin-key compromise.
Aave, Compound, and Morpho (current Conservative DeFi protocols) have multi-year track records without principal loss events.
Concentration in a single protocol within the Conservative bucket is the bigger risk than the bucket itself.

recent_sessions.synthesis: The committee converges mechanically on the regime read — composite 0.572, 68th percentile, tenth consecutive risk_on — but all three voices treat the print as unratified: the 93-point three-panel range is the widest logged on this subject, and the on-chain panel crossed below the 10th today after seven sessions sub-35, the exact load case /blog/regime-conservative-aggressive built the conservative composite to absorb. On allocation, the 95/5/0/0 vault shape holds uncontested for a sixth session, but the Agent Tokens sleeve splits the room again: Athena trims to 2-3% citing the on-chain sub-10 print as the conservative composite's trigger condition, while Woon and the operator hold the 5% mandate, the operator naming the absence of a governance artifact and the sub-deviation-threshold composite. The contested call remains the 33.7% WETH position — six sessions without a named flywheel thesis or tx-hash — which all three agree is settled by rotating ~half into SS1/SS2 and finally carving the six-sessions-overdue 1-2% USDC ops-runway tranche.

The committee converged on the regime mechanics — composite 0.599, 79th percentile, ninth straight risk_on session — but read the same 70-point panel spread and sixth consecutive sub-35 on-chain print as evidence the composite is not ratified by its underlying structure, with macro and factor carrying the print alone. The 95/5/0/0 vault shape held uncontested for a fifth session, but the Agent Tokens sleeve split the room again: Athena trimmed to 3% citing on-chain dissent as a signal the conservative composite was built to act on, while Woon and the operator held the 5% cap, framing a second caution layer as double-counting a haircut already priced in. The contested call shifted decisively to the 31.3% WETH position — now four sessions without a named flywheel thesis or tx-hash — where all three voices converged that rotating roughly half into Conservative DeFi via SS1/SS2 and finally carving the five-sessions-overdue 1-2% USDC ops-runway tranche would settle the next move.

The committee converged mechanically on the regime read — composite 0.603, 82nd percentile, eighth consecutive risk_on session — but all three voices flagged the same two structural concerns: a 60-point panel spread with on-chain dissenting at the 35th for the fifth logged session, and a composite trajectory rolling from 0.631 to 0.603 over six sessions, with macro carrying the print alone. On allocation, the 95/5/0/0 vault shape is uncontested for a fourth session, but the Agent Tokens sleeve splits the room again: Athena trims to 3-4% citing conservative-composite logic in panel-divergent regimes, while Woon and the operator hold the 5% cap, the operator framing any trim as unauthorized deviation absent a governance signal. The newly contested call is the 26.8% WETH position — Athena and the operator converge on it as discretionary directional beta without operational receipt; what would settle it is either a rotation into Conservative DeFi or a named flywheel thesis with a tx-hash, alongside the still-uncarved 1-2% USDC ops-runway tranche now four sessions overdue.
